cards.title: Vendors, with guarded payment details
cards.description: Maipa can keep a list of who you pay and how. Changing where a vendor is paid is a common fraud, so every change is its own approval: you see the details it replaces beside the new ones and how the change was verified, and every earlier version is kept. Saved account numbers are shown with only their last four digits.

cards.title: Fix: "today" means your today when recording a decision
cards.description: Late in the day, asking Maipa to record a decision to review today was refused as being in the past, because the date was taken from a clock set to a different time zone. The date now comes from your own computer.

cards.title: Decisions you want to come back to
cards.description: When you decide something that should be looked at again, such as holding off on a hire or revisiting prices, Maipa can record it with your reasons and a review date. Ask what needs your attention and Maipa tells you which decisions are due. When one is settled, you approve closing it with what came of it. Decisions are notes beside your books and change no record.

cards.title: Budgets, and how you are doing against them
cards.description: Tell Maipa what you expect to earn and spend each month and approve it as your budget. Ask how you are doing and Maipa compares your books with the budget account by account: what is over, what is under and by how much. Accounts you set no budget for are shown as unbudgeted, not as zero. A budget never changes your books.

cards.title: Key figures that explain themselves
cards.description: Ask Maipa how the business is doing and it now answers from a fixed set of key figures: revenue, expenses, net income, margin, revenue change, cash, usable cash, cash runway, assets, liabilities and net worth. Each comes with what it means and the statement line it ties to. When a figure cannot be worked out from your books, Maipa says so and why instead of estimating.

cards.title: Updated workflow and form tooling
cards.description: Maipa now uses the latest published version of the toolkit that lets it edit workflows and forms with you. Nothing changes in how you work; workflow lists Maipa reads are now in the format current AI tools expect.

cards.title: See your cash ahead beside the chat
cards.description: Ask Maipa to show your cash forecast. A panel lists usable cash for each of the next 13 weeks from your books and, if you have a cash plan, with the plan or a what-if beside it. It marks the lowest week, warns when cash goes below zero, and lists what moves each week and what you have planned.

cards.title: Plan ahead and try what-ifs
cards.description: Tell Maipa about cash you expect or intend, such as an invoice you are waiting on, payroll, or a purchase, and approve adding it to your cash plan. The 13-week look ahead then shows your books and your plan side by side. Give a what-if its own name, like hiring someone, and ask how cash looks with it. Plans never change your books or statements.

cards.title: Usable cash and a 13-week look ahead
cards.description: Ask Maipa how your cash looks over the next 13 weeks. It starts from the cash you can actually use, week by week, using what is already in your books: posted entries, entries waiting for your approval and recurring entries. You can approve setting an account aside, such as tax savings, so it is not counted as usable. Planned sales and bills not yet entered are not included, and Maipa says so.

cards.title: Consolidated totals for grouped businesses
cards.description: Tell Maipa which accounts hold dealings between your grouped businesses, such as loans or charges to each other, and approve the list once. Combined reports then add consolidated totals without those accounts. If one business recorded something the other did not, Maipa shows the difference instead of calling the figures consolidated.

cards.title: See several businesses together
cards.description: If you keep books for more than one business in the same currency, ask Maipa to group them. Maipa can then report income, expenses, assets, liabilities and cash for each business side by side with the total. Amounts the businesses owe each other, or sell to each other, are not removed from the total yet, and Maipa says so.

cards.title: Fix: released statements are readable in the side panel
cards.description: The released statements panel squeezed seven columns into the narrow panel, so amounts broke across lines. Each release is now its own block with its period, status and figures listed one per line.

cards.title: See your released statements
cards.description: Ask Maipa to show your released statements. A panel beside the chat lists each release with its period and key figures, and says whether it still matches the books, is out of date, or was replaced by a newer release.

cards.title: Fix: Maipa can ask for every kind of change again
cards.description: Over the last few updates, Maipa's list of the changes it can ask you to approve had grown too long and its end was cut off. Maipa could no longer see how to ask for opening balances, closing or reopening a period, confirming account setup, or releasing statements, and had to guess. The list is now short and complete, and a refused request tells Maipa what was expected.

cards.title: Released statements
cards.description: Once a period is closed, ask Maipa to release its statements. You approve the key figures, and the income statement, balance sheet and cash flow are kept exactly as they stood. If the books change afterwards, Maipa says the release is out of date and what differs, and you can approve a new one.

cards.title: Workflows on a schedule
cards.description: Ask Maipa to run a published workflow every day, every week or every month at an hour you choose. You approve the schedule once; Maipa then starts each run by itself, once per time, and stops if your access is removed. Workflows still cannot change your books.

cards.title: Accruals that undo themselves
cards.description: For a cost or income that belongs to one month but is billed in the next, Maipa can ask you once to post the entry at month end and its exact opposite on the date you choose. Each month then shows only what belongs to it.

cards.title: Recurring entries
cards.description: Tell Maipa about an entry that repeats every month, such as rent or a subscription, and approve it once. When a month comes due, Maipa drafts that month's entry and asks you to approve posting it. Nothing posts by itself, and the same month is never entered twice.

cards.title: See the month-end checklist beside the chat
cards.description: Maipa can open the close checklist next to the conversation: which months are closed, and for the date you want to close, every draft, unposted statement line and unreconciled statement still open. It reads your books live and changes nothing.

cards.title: A month-end checklist before you close
cards.description: Ask Maipa whether a month is ready to close. It checks for draft entries, statement lines without a posted entry, bank statements that are not reconciled, and the soundness of every entry, and tells you exactly what is outstanding. Closing the books stays your decision.
